featured.title: Saudi Pipeline Shutdown Adds New Pressure to Global Oil Supplies
featured.content: Saudi Arabia has temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack that Saudi and Iraqi officials said originated from Iraqi territory. The 1,200-kilometre pipeline has been carrying around 4–5 million barrels per day and provides Saudi Arabia with an alternative route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Its closure comes as shipping through Hormuz remains severely restricted and Houthi forces tighten their position near the Bab el-Mandeb.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Shuts East-West Oil Pipeline After Drone Attack
articles.content: Saudi Arabia has temporarily closed its East-West oil pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack believed to have originated from Iraq. The pipeline stretches about 1,200 kilometres across the Arabian Peninsula and has been carrying around 4–5 million barrels of oil per day. The shutdown adds another source of uncertainty to an already disrupted global energy market.

articles.title: Iraq Dismisses Military Commander After Saudi Drone Attack
articles.content: Iraq has dismissed a military commander responsible for operations in Maysan province following investigations into drone attacks on Saudi Arabia launched from Iraqi territory. Baghdad has also taken additional security measures, including closing a major border crossing with Iran.

articles.title: Houthi Forces Seize Strategic Perim Island
articles.content: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have taken control of Perim Island at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Yemeni government sources cited by Reuters. The island sits along one of the world's most important shipping routes connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
articles.imageQuery: Perim Island Yemen Bab el Mandeb

articles.title: Two Major Energy Corridors Face Pressure
articles.content: The latest developments place simultaneous pressure on the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Disruption at both routes could force ships to take longer journeys, raise insurance and freight costs and further increase pressure on global energy prices.
articles.imageQuery: Bab el Mandeb Strait shipping tanker

articles.title: Hormuz Traffic Remains Far Below Normal
articles.content: Only seven vessels were recorded transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, compared with a recent 10-day average of 15 and a pre-conflict level of around 125 commercial vessels per day. The dramatic reduction continues to threaten the normal movement of energy and other commodities.

articles.title: Nigeria Suspends Official Parliamentary Engagements With South Africa
articles.content: Nigeria's National Assembly has suspended official parliamentary visits and participation in legislative events in South Africa over continuing concerns about anti-migrant violence affecting Nigerians and other African nationals. The measure does not stop normal government-to-government relations, but represents a significant parliamentary protest.

articles.title: Nigeria–South Africa Tensions Continue Over Anti-Migrant Violence
articles.content: Reuters reports that 98 Nigerians have died in mob or hate-related incidents in South Africa since 2022, while 1,695 Nigerians have been voluntarily evacuated during 2026. The Nigerian parliamentary decision adds fresh diplomatic pressure between two of Africa's largest economies.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Remains Central to Nigeria's Energy Strategy
articles.content: Dangote Refinery continues to attract attention as global oil prices rise. The refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October, equivalent to around 520,000 barrels per day. Greater domestic refining could help reduce Nigeria's reliance on imported refined petroleum products.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Passes 7,000 Confirmed Cases
articles.content: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 7,022 confirmed cases and 3,398 deaths, according to the latest government figures reported by Reuters. The outbreak has now spread across seven provinces and has reached South Ubangi in northwestern Congo.
articles.imageQuery: Ebola healthcare workers Democratic Republic Congo

articles.title: South Ubangi Becomes Latest Ebola Front
articles.content: The detection of Ebola in South Ubangi is particularly concerning because the province is far from the original epicentre. Health officials have begun contact tracing, but the World Health Organization has warned that shortages of trained personnel, partners and funding are hampering the response.

articles.title: Uganda Prepares for King Oyo's Burial Amid Succession Dispute
articles.content: Uganda is preparing to bury King Oyo Nyimba of the Tooro Kingdom after his death at age 34. A royal clan committee has selected his cousin Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma as successor, but the late king's mother and sister say his will identified a son as heir. The dispute has created uncertainty around the traditional succession process.
articles.imageQuery: King Oyo Uganda Tooro Kingdom funeral

articles.title: Federal Judge Blocks Civil-Service Political Loyalty Question
articles.content: A federal judge in Boston has blocked the Trump administration from continuing to ask applicants for US civil-service positions to answer a political 'loyalty' question. The judge found that the policy likely conflicted with protections requiring a merit-based and non-partisan federal workforce.

articles.title: More Than 70,000 Federal Job Listings Included the Question
articles.content: The disputed question appeared in more than 70,000 federal job postings, according to lawyers representing government employee unions. The administration had argued that the question was optional and intended to assess applicants' commitment to government policy, while unions argued that it improperly tested political views.
articles.imageQuery: US civil service government workers Washington

articles.title: Trump Open to Chinese Automakers Building Cars in America
articles.content: President Donald Trump says he would be willing to allow Chinese automakers to build vehicles in the United States provided they employ American workers. He said he would not support Chinese companies building cars in Mexico and exporting them into the US market. The proposal faces opposition from US lawmakers and domestic automobile manufacturers.
articles.imageQuery: Chinese electric car factory United States

articles.title: European Markets Watch Oil Shock Closely
articles.content: European markets remain exposed to the latest Middle East energy shock. Higher oil and shipping costs could keep inflation elevated and complicate decisions by central banks about interest rates and economic growth.

articles.title: Critical Infrastructure Remains a Security Concern
articles.content: European governments continue to monitor potential threats to undersea cables and other critical infrastructure. The latest Middle East developments are adding to wider concerns about the vulnerability of strategic infrastructure during periods of geopolitical tension.

articles.title: Asian Economies Face New Energy Risks
articles.content: Asian economies remain exposed to the energy crisis because many rely heavily on imported oil. Prolonged disruption around Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb could raise fuel, manufacturing and transport costs across the region.

articles.title: Global Oil Supply Faces Fresh Pressure
articles.content: The Saudi pipeline shutdown comes after Saudi crude supply had already fallen sharply. The International Energy Agency estimated Saudi crude supply at around 6 million barrels per day in August, the lowest level in more than three decades.

articles.title: Oil and Shipping Costs Keep Inflation in Focus
articles.content: Global businesses are facing higher energy and freight costs as the Middle East conflict disrupts major shipping corridors. Prolonged disruption could feed into transport, food, manufacturing and household expenses well beyond the region.

The pipeline normally carries around 4–5 million barrels per day. At the same time, Iran-aligned Houthi forces have seized strategic Perim Island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Nigeria is facing a diplomatic dispute with South Africa over anti-migrant violence, while the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 7,000 confirmed cases. Uganda is preparing to bury King Oyo amid a royal succession dispute, while a US federal judge has blocked a controversial political loyalty question for civil-service applicants.
